notes_for_us: One shape cannot hold a lobby and a match map. space-staged is exactly this pattern and routes P4; warren-looping describes the match map and routes P6. The prompt needs both halves and emit has one shape slot, so the lobby survived only as an option plus a note.

The 1 vs All preset carries gate-escape while the genre notes say a timer-win mode must not have an exit. Both statements are in the same file and this prompt sits on top of both, so the preset contradicts itself rather than the prompt.

The lobby countdown timer is the clearest world-space UI I have hit: geometry the image model must draw that displays a number, and no option covers it. tracker-leaderboard is the nearest row and it is a wall for scores.
Puzzles that are obstacles rather than progression gates have no home. gate-solve and gate-progression both gate, and the prompt says explicitly that these do not.

notes_for_us: Nine words in, four picks out, three of them from the preset. The Incremental Simulator preset assumes a shop and purchase gates that nothing in the prompt implies, and step 3 offers no test for when a prompt is too thin to carry a preset at all — the alternative on offer is preset null, which loses the shape too.

collectible-nodes goes to layout in every genre that lists it, which means the plant, tree or vein the resource sits on is never drawn. For a prompt whose entire scene is berry bushes, the only routed pick contributes nothing to the image.
Simulation has ten presets and none of them is a small gathering loop with no economy. The closest, Sandbox, is about building; the next, Mining and Extraction, brings a whole underground layer.

checkpoint-respawn comes from the preset and the prompt contradicts it outright: going off the path sends you back to the top, so mid-course recovery points would remove the stated failure cost. Kept as instructed but it must be dropped before build.

The path itself has no option row — lane-corridor is painted dividers and barrier-guardrail physically blocks, and this path is defined by the drop either side — so the road ships as free text while the P6 on the shape still guarantees it is one followable route.
Steering-only control and a rolling object as the player are mechanics, but they also invalidate the avatar jump and walk baselines the P6 validator uses.

notes_for_us: The player is a tyre. Nothing in the network can say the controlled thing is not an avatar, and the whole P6 validation the genre exists for is calibrated on avatar walk speed and jump limits from Build.md Part I. The route will be checked against numbers that do not apply.

Downhill Descent bundles checkpoint-respawn, and a descent whose stated punishment is restarting from the top is a common enough kind of game that the preset fights its own premise. Same pattern as the 1 vs All escape gate elsewhere in this batch: presets carrying the recovery or exit feature that the mode deliberately omits.

Racing has options for painted lanes, guardrails, turnarounds and off-track penalties, but no row for the road itself. On a point-to-point descent the road is the entire build, and it can only be expressed as the shape plus free text.
